claims.text: Leather is animal skin or hide treated with chemicals to preserve it for use in clothing, footwear, handbags, furniture, tools and sports equipment.

quotes.quote: animalskins and hides that have been treated with chemicals to preserve them and make them suitable for use as clothing, footwear, handbags, furniture, tools, and sports equipment.

claims.text: The term hide designates the skin of larger animals such as cows and horses, as distinct from the skins of smaller animals such as calves and kids.

quotes.quote: The term hide is used to designate the skin of larger animals (e.g., cowhide or horsehide), whereas refers to that of smaller animals (e.g., calfskin or kidskin).

claims.text: Tanning is the chemical treatment that converts otherwise perishable skin into a stable, non-decaying material, and it is the most important chemical step in leather making.

quotes.quote: The preservation process employed is a chemical treatment called tanning, which converts the otherwise perishable skin to a stable and nondecaying material.
the tanning process is the most important chemical process that converts animal skins into leather

claims.text: Tanning agents include vegetable tannins from sources such as tree bark, mineral salts such as chromium sulfate, and fish or animal oils.

quotes.quote: Tanning agents include vegetable tannins (from sources such as tree bark), mineral salts (such as chromiumsulfate), and fish or animal oils.

claims.text: Leathers are traditionally made by three types of tanning, vegetable, chrome and syntan tanning, though newer sustainable methods have since been developed.

quotes.quote: Traditionally, leathers are processed by the three types of tanning methods including vegetable tanning, chrome tanning and syntan tanning but recently the tanning processes are quite improved with the development of various sustainable tanning methods.

claims.text: Kolhapuri chappals are handmade open footwear made of vegetable-tanned leather with traditional techniques and tools.

quotes.quote: Kolhapuri Chappal are handmade open Indian footwear made of tanned vegetable leather produced using traditional technique and tools.

claims.text: The Kolhapuri GI application states that the chappal is made completely and exclusively from bag-tanned vegetable leather.

quotes.locator: Application 169, I) Method of Production, p. 8
quotes.quote: The Kolhapuri chappal is completely and exclusively made from bag tanned vegetable leather.

claims.text: Tholu bommalata, literally the dance of the leather puppets, is the shadow theatre tradition of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and part of Karnataka.

quotes.quote: literally means the dance (attam, ata) of the leather (tholu) puppets (bommalu)
Tholu bommalata is the shadow theatre tradition of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and part of Karnataka.

claims.text: Togalu gombeyata is a traditional shadow theatre of Karnataka whose name joins togalu, leather, with gombeyata, figure, doll, dance and performance.

quotes.quote: Traditional shadow theatre from Karnataka in south-west India. Togalu signifies "leather" and gombeyata "figure, doll, dance and performance".

claims.text: Santiniketan leather goods are a byproduct of Rabindranath Tagore's Rural Reconstruction initiative at Visva-Bharati University.

quotes.quote: Santiniketan leather goods are a byproduct of Rabindranath Tagore's Rural Reconstruction initiative at the Visva Bharati University.
The products are named Santiniketan Leather Goods as they were originated in this cluster under rural development program of VisvaBharati university of Santiniketan

claims.text: Kanpur Saddlery craftsmen make saddles, harnesses and other equestrian equipment from leather obtained from local tanneries.

quotes.quote: High-quality leather, obtained from local tanneries, is crafted meticulously to create saddles, harnesses and other equestrian equipment.
existence of manufacturers, craftsmen and raw material, i.e. leather, at the same place.

claims.text: Finished leather is fashioned into shoes and boots, apparel, belts, upholstery, suede goods, saddles, gloves, luggage, purses and recreational equipment.

quotes.quote: The leather is then ready to be fashioned into any of a multitude of products. These include shoes and boots, outer apparel, belts, upholstery materials, suede products, saddles, gloves, luggage and purses, and recreational equipment

claims.text: Chamar names a widespread caste of northern India whose hereditary occupation is tanning leather, from the Sanskrit charmakara, skin worker.

quotes.quote: widespreadcaste in northern India whose hereditary occupation is tanning leather; the name is derived from the Sanskrit word charmakara ("skin worker").

claims.text: The BBC notes that Chamar is a pejorative caste term for Dalits, formerly known as untouchables, who work with animal hides.

quotes.quote: Chamar is a pejorative caste term used to describe Dalits (formerly known as untouchables) who work with animal hides.

claims.text: Chamars include groups that skin and dispose of animal carcasses, tanners, and makers of shoes and other leather goods.

quotes.quote: Cham?rs include groups that skin and dispose of animal carcasses, tanners, and makers of shoes and other leather goods.

claims.text: Sahapedia notes that animal leather and its manufacturers are considered impure in India, as are the low-caste puppeteers who handle it.

quotes.quote: Animal leather and its manufacturers are considered impure in India as are the low caste puppeteers handling it.

claims.text: Leather making has been practised for more than 7,000 years, and fresh skins were dried in the sun and softened by pounding in animal fats and brains.

quotes.quote: Leather making is an ancient art that has been practiced for more than 7,000 years. Fresh skins were dried in the sun, softened by pounding in animal fats and brains, and preserved by salting and smoking.

claims.text: The primitive preservation process dried raw hides and skins in the sun, and vegetable extracts were used to convert them into leather.

quotes.quote: The primitive preservation process involved drying the raw hides/skins in the sun and vegetable extracts were used to convert the raw hides/skins to leather.

claims.text: Vegetable tanning is the oldest method of turning hides and skins into leather, and it is still important.

quotes.quote: Vegetable tanning is the oldest tanning method, developed to produce leather from hides/skins.
Vegetable tanning, which is the oldest of tanning methods, is still important.

claims.text: The first chrome tanning process was described by Professor Knapp in 1858 and first brought into commercial prominence by Dr Heinzerling about 1878.

quotes.quote: The first chrome tanning process was described by Professor Knapp in 1858 in a paper on "Die Natur und Wesen der Gerberie," but was first brought into commercial prominence by Dr Heinzerling about 1878

claims.text: Britannica's eleventh edition described chrome tanning as almost the most important method of light leather dressing, with a prominent place in heavy leather as well.

quotes.quote: Now chrome tanning is almost the most important method of light leather dressing, and has also taken a prominent place in the heavy department

claims.text: Vedic literature holds numerous references to leather goods such as bags, clothing, bowstrings, reins and shields, and even instructions for preparing skins.

quotes.quote: There are numerous references in the Vedic literature to leather goods (e.g., leather bags, clothing, bowstrings, reins, leather shields, etc.), and even instructions for the preparing of skins for manufacture.

claims.text: One encyclopedia account holds that tanners and leatherworkers were clearly an important occupational group in early Aryan society, though likely of inferior social standing.

quotes.quote: Tanners and leatherworkers were clearly an important occupational group in early Aryan society.

quotes.quote: Bag tanning was also practiced extensively in Punjab (Jalandhar), West Bengal (Kolkatta) and U.P. (Kanpur) in the past.

quotes.quote: CAWNPORE, or Kanpur, a city and district of British India in the Allahabad division of the United Provinces.

quotes.quote: The earliest records of Kolhapur sandals date back to the 12th Century.

quotes.quote: The Santiniketan leather goods has a fascinating origin, with Rabindranath Tagore introducing and promoting this craftwork in 1932.

quotes.quote: Shadow puppetry in South India has a very long history-it was indeed already popular under Satavahana and Chalukya dynasties (4th - 6th centuries AD).

claims.text: Shadow theatre probably spread from South India to South East Asia and beyond during that period, with local styles developing from Indonesia to China.

quotes.quote: It is probably during this period that shadow theatre from South India spread to South East Asia and beyond, and local styles developed in Indonesia, Burma, Thailand, Malaysia, Japan and China.

claims.text: Neelakantha Panditha, a 12th-century commentator of the Mahabharata, reports that shadow plays with leather puppets were popular in South India in his time.

quotes.quote: Neelakantha Panditha (a 12th century commentator of the Mahabharata) reports that at that time in South India, shadow plays with leather puppets were popular

quotes.quote: According to historical sources, in the 17th century, groups of performers from Maharashtra moved to the southern regions of the Indian subcontinent

quotes.quote: The puppeteers are from the Killikyeta tribal group that came from Maharashtra at least two centuries ago and settled in different regions of Southern India, particularly in Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

claims.text: The Killikyeta still speak Aare Marathi, a dialect based on archaic Marathi that the population of the southern states does not understand.

quotes.quote: They still speak Aare (Aré) Marathi, a dialect based on archaic Marathi, which is not understood by the population of the southern states.

claims.text: Cowhide is mostly used for manufacturing leather goods, while buffalo, goat and sheep hides are also used but relatively little.

quotes.quote: Cowhide is mostly used in manufacturing leather goods. Buffalo, goat and sheep hides are also used but their use is relatively low.

quotes.quote: the more common leathers come from seven main groups: cattle, including calves and oxen; sheep and lambs; goats and kids; equine animals, including horses, mules, and zebras; buffalo; pigs and hogs; and such aquatic animals as seals, walrus, whales, and alligators.

claims.text: Leather is made from animal hides and skins, which are a by-product of the meat industry.

quotes.quote: Leather is made from animal hides/skins, which are a by-product of the meat industry.

claims.text: Of a mammal hide's three layers, the corium, the thick central layer, is used to make leather once the other two are removed.

quotes.quote: The hides of mammals are composed of three layers: epidermis, a thin outer layer; corium, or dermis, the thick central layer; and a subcutaneous fatty layer. The corium is used to make leather after the two sandwiching layers have been removed.

quotes.quote: Buffalo hides - Green/wet salted/ weighing about 25-30 kg. each. Cow hides, calf skins of buff and cow are also used.

quotes.quote: Vegetable tanning material: Babulbark (Acacia Arabica) and myrobalan nuts (Terminalia Chebula).
Bag tanned leather, using babulbark and myrobalan fruits.
filled with hot water infused with myrobalan nuts (hirda) and pieces of babul bark.

quotes.quote: Myrobalans are the fruit of an Indian tree.
They are a very light-coloured material, containing from 27 % to 38 % of tannin; they deposit much "bloom," ferment fairly rapidly, supplying acidity, and yield a mellow leather.

claims.text: East India tanned sheep and goat skins, called Persians, were tanned with turwar bark and cassia bark and impregnated with sesame oil, even to 30%.

quotes.quote: Great quantities of "Persian" (East India tanned) sheep and goat are now dressed as moroccos and for innumerable other purposes
The goods are tanned with turwar bark and cassia bark, besides being impregnated with sesame oil, even to the extent of 30%.

quotes.quote: East Indian hides are known as kips, and are supposed to be, and should be, the hides of yearling cattle.
They come from a small breed of ox, and have an extremely tight grain

quotes.quote: Puppeteers-who are also the manufacturers-mostly use the hide of goats, and occasionally buffalo or deer skin.

claims.text: Togalu gombeyata figures used to be carved from doe skin, but goat skin is now used.

quotes.quote: In the past, figures used to be carved from doe skin but now goat skin is used.

quotes.quote: Such vegetable-tanned leather pieces retain embossed imprints permanently, making them an ideal raw material for this craft. The leather pieces come from sheep and goat skins.
trays, and domestic objects-made from vegetable-tanned goat and sheepskin and decorated through embossing, stencil work, and batik techniques

claims.text: Tholu bommalata leather undergoes specific treatments so that it looks like translucent stiff parchment.

quotes.quote: Tholu bommalata shadow puppets are made of leather that undergoes specific treatments in order to look like translucent stiff parchment.

claims.text: Vegetable-tanned leather takes a long time to produce, and its strength, stability and durability are inferior to those of chrome-tanned leather.

quotes.quote: The production of vegetable-tanned leather takes a long time, and the strength, stability, and durability of the leather is inferior to that of chrome-tanned leather.

claims.text: Leather is made of collagen protein polymer, a skin-derived fibrillar type I collagen material.

quotes.quote: Leather is made of collagen protein polymer, which is used in the manufacture of a variety of products including footwear, automotive upholstery, garments, and sports equipment.
Leather is a skin-derived fibrillar type I collagen material.

claims.text: Raw animal skin is 60-65% water, 30-33% protein, mostly collagen, 2-6% fat and 0.5-1.0% minerals.

quotes.quote: Raw animal skin is composed of 60-65% water, 30-33% protein (mostly collagen), 2-6% fat and 0.5-1.0% minerals

claims.text: Fresh hides contain between 60 and 70 percent water and 30 to 35 percent protein, about 85 percent of the protein being collagen.

quotes.quote: Fresh hides contain between 60 and 70 percent water by weight and 30 to 35 percent protein. About 85 percent of the protein is collagen, a fibrous protein held together by chemical bonds.

claims.text: Tanning preserves the hide, strengthening it and limiting degradation, especially when wet, by compacting its collagen fibres, which makes the leather imputrescible.

quotes.quote: The purpose of tanning is to preserve the hide/skin, enhance its strength and make it durable by limiting degradation, especially when the leather is wet by compacting collagen fibres in the leather, making it imputrescible.

claims.text: Leather making uses acids, bases, salts, enzymes and tannins to dissolve fats and non-fibrous proteins and strengthen the bonds between collagen fibres.

quotes.quote: Basically, leather making is the science of using acids, bases, salts, enzymes, and tannins to dissolvefats and nonfibrous proteins and strengthen the bonds between the collagen fibres.

claims.text: Tanning takes its name from tannin, the agent that displaces water from between the hide's protein fibres and cements these fibres together.

quotes.quote: The tanning process derives its name from tannin (tannic acid), the agent that displaces water from the interstices of the hide's protein fibres and cements these fibres together.

claims.text: Vegetable tanning uses tannin extracted from barks, nuts, leaves, fruits and wood, a polyphenolic agent known to bind to protein.

quotes.quote: In the vegetable tanning process, tannin extracted from barks, nuts, leaves, fruits, and wood is used. Tannin is a polyphenolic agent known to bind to protein.

claims.text: The weakly anionic phenolic groups of vegetable tannins form ionic bonds with collagen's amino groups and hydrogen bonds with its carboxyl groups.

quotes.quote: The weakly anionic phenolic groups form ionic bonding with the amino groups and hydrogen bonding with the carboxyl groups of collagens.

claims.text: Vegetable tanning is carried out at pH 3 to 4, where weakly anionic polyphenols are attracted to the cationic amino groups of collagen.

quotes.quote: Natural polyphenols (e.g., tara and mimosa tannins) have plenty of phenolic groups that make them weakly anionic, and tanning is carried out at pH 3 to 4 as they are attracted to the cationic amino groups of collagens.

claims.text: Tannin molecular weights of a few hundred to a few thousand allow tannins to be absorbed into collagen fibres.

quotes.quote: The molecular weight of tannin is a few hundred to a few thousand, allowing absorption into collagen fibres.

claims.text: Tannins fall into two classes, catechol and pyrogallol tannins, and the finest leather results are obtained by blending the two.

quotes.quote: There are two distinctive classes of tannins, viz. catechol and pyrogallol tannins.
pyrogallol tannins, however, yield an excellent leather; but the finest results are obtained by blending the two.

claims.text: Pyrogallol tannins give a blue-black colour or precipitate with ferric salts, and catechol tannins a green-black.

quotes.quote: Pyrogallol tannins give a blue-black coloration or precipitate with ferric salts, and catechol tannins a green-black

claims.text: In the classification of tanning materials, myrobalans, Terminalia chebula, fall among the pyrogallols and gambier among the catechols.

quotes.quote: Pyrogallols. | Catechols. | | Myrobalans (Terminalia Chebula). | Gambier (Uncaria Gambir).

claims.text: Chrome tanning soaks the delimed, dehaired hide in a Cr(III) salt solution, preferably basic chromium sulphate, Cr4(SO4)5(OH)2, less toxic than hexavalent chromium.

quotes.quote: In the chrome tanning method, the delimed and dehaired hide/skin is soaked in a Cr(III) salt solution, preferably basic chromium sulphate (BCS) with a chemical formula of Cr4(SO4)5(OH)2, which is less toxic than the highly toxic hexavalent form of chromium.

claims.text: Cationic chromium binds to the carboxylic groups of collagen's amino acids, and amino nitrogen forms ligands with chromium, together forming a metal complex.

quotes.quote: For example, cationic Cr binds to carboxylic groups of amino acids of collagen, and the nitrogen of amino groups of collagen forms ligands with Cr, combinedly forming a metal complex with amino acids of collagen.

claims.text: Chrome tanning is carried out at a quite low pH, 2 to 3, to minimise the size of the polychromium complex.

quotes.quote: Cr tanning is carried out at a quite low pH (2 to 3) to minimise the size of the polychromium complex

claims.text: After chrome tanning, sodium carbonate raises the bath to pH 3.8 to 4.0 and heating up to 40 °C forms a strong bond with the collagen.

quotes.quote: After the tanning process, sodium carbonate is added to the tanning bath to raise the pH to 3.8 to 4.0, the pH increase is accompanied by an increase in heating up to 40 °C, forming a strong bond with the collagen.

lede.text: Leather is animal skin or hide that tanning, a chemical treatment with vegetable tannins, mineral salts such as chromium sulfate, or oils, converts from perishable skin into a stable, non-decaying material.

The category's footwear includes Kolhapuri chappals of Maharashtra and Karnataka, which the GI application says are made only of bag-tanned leather, embroidered Chamba chappals and Punjabi juttis, and its other articles include Kanpur saddlery, Santiniketan leather goods and leather shadow puppets.

Britannica describes the Chamars, a caste term the BBC notes is pejorative, as a caste whose hereditary occupation is tanning leather, adding that while many still practise that craft, many more are part of the broader agricultural and urban labour force; in the Kolhapuri trade, The Hindu reported in 2017, the Dhors run the tanneries and the Chambhars make the chappals.

Kolhapuri chappals are made from bag-tanned buffalo and cow hides, Kanpur saddlery from vegetable-tanned buffalo leather, tholu bommalata puppets mostly from goat hide treated to look like translucent stiff parchment, and Santiniketan goods from vegetable-tanned sheep and goat skins that retain embossed imprints.

sentences.text: Leather is used for clothing, footwear, handbags, furniture, tools and sports equipment, and finished leather is fashioned into shoes and boots, belts, upholstery, saddles, gloves, luggage and purses.
Leathers are traditionally made by vegetable, chrome and syntan tanning, though newer sustainable methods have since been developed.

Among footwear, Kolhapuri chappals are handmade open footwear of vegetable-tanned leather, Chamba chappals are intricately embroidered leather chappals handmade in Chamba town, and Punjab Newsline reported in 2007 that Punjabi juttis, known for their embroidery and varied hues, were made on a large scale in Amritsar.

Among other articles, Kanpur Saddlery craftsmen make saddles, harnesses and other equestrian equipment from leather obtained from local tanneries, and Santiniketan leather goods are a byproduct of Rabindranath Tagore's Rural Reconstruction initiative at Visva-Bharati University.

CCRT says India has the richest variety of shadow puppets, flat figures cut from leather treated to be translucent, a tradition that survives in Orissa, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

Tholu bommalata, literally the dance of the leather puppets, is the shadow theatre tradition of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and part of Karnataka, and togalu gombeyata is a traditional shadow theatre of Karnataka.

Chamars include groups that skin and dispose of animal carcasses, tanners, and makers of shoes and other leather goods; in Andhra Pradesh the leather workers belong to the Madiga caste, and Chamars are called Regar in Rajasthan and Bhambi in Maharashtra.
Sahapedia notes that animal leather and its manufacturers are considered impure in India, as are the low-caste puppeteers who handle it.
Leather making has been practised for more than 7,000 years, and vegetable tanning is the oldest method of turning hides and skins into leather.
Vedic literature holds numerous references to leather goods such as bags, clothing, bowstrings, reins and shields, and even instructions for preparing skins.

The first chrome tanning process was described by Professor Knapp in 1858 and brought into commercial prominence by Dr Heinzerling about 1878, and Britannica's eleventh edition described chrome tanning as almost the most important method of light leather dressing.

The Kolhapuri GI application, from the story of Basaveswara and Haralayya, dates footwear made by Chamars from bag-tanned leather to the 12th century, and the BBC dates the earliest records of Kolhapur sandals to the 12th century.

The Kolhapuri GI application says bag tanning was once practised extensively in Jalandhar, Kolkata and Kanpur, and Britannica's eleventh edition described Cawnpore, or Kanpur, as a great emporium for harness, shoes and other leather-work.

Quoting Tirthankar Roy, GI Journal 54 says Kanpur was chosen in 1867 as the site for a government harness and saddlery factory, and that Cooper Allen, started in 1880, soon became the source of the entire Indian army's boots, shoes and saddlery.

Shadow puppetry in South India was already popular under the Satavahana and Chalukya dynasties, which Sahapedia dates to the 4th to 6th centuries AD, and in the 17th century groups of performers from Maharashtra moved south and performed in Telugu.

Sources differ on Santiniketan leatherwork: India's tourism ministry site says Rabindranath Tagore introduced it in 1932, while a Small Industries Service Institute study says Rathindranath Tagore and Protima Devi led the Visva-Bharati work from which it originated.
Leather is made from animal hides and skins, which are a by-product of the meat industry, and the corium, the thick central layer of a mammal's hide, is used to make leather.
Cowhide is mostly used for manufacturing leather goods, while buffalo, goat and sheep hides are also used but relatively little.
Kolhapuri bag tanning uses green or wet-salted buffalo hides of about 25-30 kg each, with cow hides and calf skins, tanned with babul bark and myrobalan nuts (hirda).
The Kanpur Saddlery GI statement says its harness and saddlery goods use vegetable-tanned buffalo leather that is also manufactured in Kanpur.
Santiniketan goods are made from vegetable-tanned sheep and goat skins that retain embossed imprints permanently, a leather known as E.I. tanned leather and manufactured only in Tamil Nadu.

Tholu bommalata puppeteers mostly use goat hide and occasionally buffalo or deer skin, treated to look like translucent stiff parchment, while togalu gombeyata figures, once carved from doe skin, now use goat skin.
Myrobalans, the fruit of an Indian tree, contain from 27 % to 38 % of tannin, and East India tanned sheep and goat skins were tanned with turwar bark and cassia bark.
Vegetable-tanned leather takes a long time to produce, and its strength, stability and durability are inferior to those of chrome-tanned leather.
Leather is made of collagen protein polymer, and tanning preserves the hide by compacting its collagen fibres, which makes the leather imputrescible.
Tanning takes its name from tannin, the agent that displaces water from between the hide's protein fibres and cements these fibres together.

Vegetable tannins are polyphenolic agents extracted from barks, nuts, leaves, fruits and wood, whose weakly anionic phenolic groups form ionic bonds with collagen's amino groups and hydrogen bonds with its carboxyl groups, at pH 3 to 4.
Tannins fall into two classes, catechol and pyrogallol tannins, myrobalans falling among the pyrogallols, and the finest leather results are obtained by blending the two.

Chrome tanning soaks the hide in a Cr(III) salt solution, preferably basic chromium sulphate, Cr4(SO4)5(OH)2, at a low pH of 2 to 3, and cationic chromium binds to the carboxylic groups of collagen to form a metal complex.
A review of tanning chemistry, naming no country, states that 90% of hides and skins are chrome tanned and the rest vegetable tanned, and chrome-tanned wet blue leather holds 4% to 5% chromium.
Chrome tanning produces effluent with elevated levels of Cr(III), some of which converts to Cr(VI), and chrome tanning is therefore restricted in the developed world.
Raw hides or skins shrink very easily at about 55 °C, while chrome-tanned leather shows shrinkage temperatures higher than 100 °C.
Goatskin tanned with 8% pala indigo plant tannin reached a shrinkage temperature of only 70 °C.
Britannica's eleventh edition described chrome-tanned leather as able to stand boiling water, whereas vegetable-tanned leather was completely destroyed at 70° C.
Leather's grain is made of fibres 1 μm in diameter that interweave into a smooth surface, while its corium of 100 μm fibres is built more loosely.
In togalu gombeyata the light source, once an oil lamp, later a hurricane lamp and now a neon, sits between the puppeteer and the leather figures.
The modern commercial leather-making process has three basic phases: preparation for tanning, tanning, and processing tanned leather.
A hide begins to decompose within hours of an animal's death, so it is cured before reaching the tannery, where it is soaked, limed to loosen the hair, washed, delimed, bated and pickled.
Vegetable tanning soaks hides in increasingly strong tan liquors for weeks or months, while mineral tanning, with chromium salt its most widely used agent, can shorten tanning to days or even hours.
After tanning, leather is dried, dyed and worked with blended oils and greases to make it softer, stronger and better able to shed water.
Leather is dried to about 14 percent moisture and then reconditioned with damp sawdust to a uniform moisture content of 20 percent.
Kolhapuri chappals are known for a decorative woven pattern fixed over their upper bands, and Chamba chappals are adorned with golden and coloured embroidery.
Punjabi juttis are made of soft leather with artistic work, their traditional embroidery being teela, zeri wali and sundi work in golden thread.
Santiniketan goods carry embossed or batik designs: embossed pieces are pressed with zinc blocks and touch dyed with spirit-based natural dyes, while batik pieces are resisted with gum arabic.
Santiniketan leather goods are identified by a smooth, glossy, shiny look, vibrant hues and embedded traditional motifs.
Tholu bommalata puppets measure 120 to 180 centimetres, are jointed at the waist, shoulders, elbows and knees, and are coloured on both sides, throwing coloured shadows.
CCRT describes Orissa's Ravanachhaya puppets as one-piece deer-skin figures with no joints, not coloured and so throwing opaque shadows.
Togalu gombeyata figures are tinted, not painted, and chikka theatre uses figures 20 to 30 centimetres high while dodda uses figures 30 to 120 centimetres high.

The Council for Leather Exports places India's major leather and footwear centres in states from Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh to Maharashtra, Punjab and Karnataka, among them Chennai, Ranipet, Vellore, Kolkata, Kanpur, Agra and Jalandhar.

Jajmau in north-eastern Kanpur is the major cluster of tanneries; a 2012 paper notes that CLRI records showed only 170 tanneries at Kanpur while a 2000 study found twice that number in one cluster, and a 2025 paper, citing earlier work, puts around 400 tanneries in Jajmau.
The Kolhapuri GI area comprises Sholapur, Sangli, Kolhapur and Satara districts in Maharashtra and Dharwad, Belgaum, Bagalkot and Bijapur districts in Karnataka.

The Andhra Pradesh Leather Puppetry GI application gives its area of production as Nimmalakunta in Anantapur district and Narsaraopet in Guntur district, while tholu bommalata itself spans the Telugu-speaking area beyond exact state borders.

A Small Industries Service Institute study locates the Santiniketan leather goods cluster in and around Santiniketan and Bolpur in Birbhum district, while Chamba chappals are handmade by craftsmen in Chamba town.
Togalu gombeyata performances are held in the Mysore, Mandya and Bellary regions and a few other villages of Karnataka.

India's exports of leather and leather products fell 27.58%, from US$ 5,083.76 million in 2019-20 to US$ 3,681.58 million in 2020-21, while saddlery and harness exports rose 22.94% from US$ 151.44 million to US$ 186.18 million.
India is the second largest footwear producer after China, with an annual production of 2.58 billion pairs in 2018.
Kolhapuri Chappal holds GI certificate 329 dated 11-12-2018, though the BBC reports the GI was awarded in 2019, and Chamba Chappal holds certificate 403 dated 14-09-2021.

Santiniketan Leather Goods and Andhra Pradesh Leather Puppetry were registered with certificates 90 and 93, both dated 09-09-2008, and Kanpur Saddlery's merged application 159 holds certificate 204 dated 31-03-2014, valid up to 08-02-2029.
GI Journal 38 also lists E. I. Leather, as manufactured goods, and Leather Toys of Indore, as a handicraft, among GI applications in class 18, leather and imitation of leather.
GI Journal 54 describes Kanpur's saddlery industry as highly labour-intensive and 100% export oriented, with a negligible local market.
Leather puppet makers have diversified into lampshades, wall hangings and other everyday objects, and recent decades have seen puppets produced as tourist craft.
Reporting Kolhapur artisans' charge that Prada plagiarised their designs, the BBC notes that a GI protects a name and design within India, but no binding law stops imitation abroad.

Vegetable tanning effluent is less toxic than chrome tanning effluent, while dehairing, with sodium sulphide that decomposes to toxic hydrogen sulphide gas, is the most heavily polluting tanning operation.

Kanpur's tanneries must treat their wastewater before it reaches the Common Effluent Treatment Plant at Jajmau, with a reported capacity of 36 million litres a day, which CPCB found in 2021 operating without valid consent.
In the 2021 CPCB inspection, raw tannery effluent carried total chromium of 132 mg/l against a norm of 10 mg/l, and only 117 tanneries were members of the chrome recovery plant.
Chromium dumps at Rania in Kanpur Dehat and Rakhi Mandi in Kanpur Nagar, in existence since 1976, contaminated groundwater and deprived residents of proper drinking water.

A 2012 survey found Cr (VI) in contaminated areas of Kanpur up to 390 fold higher than the permissible limit, and in 1997 the Central Pollution Control Board had reported Cr (VI) at Kanpur up to 250 times the WHO limit.
A paper on Kanpur's tanneries cites the National Green Tribunal's 2019 action against 22 tanneries, fined Rs. 280 crore for dumping chromium-laden wastewater into the Ganga.
Cr(VI) was replaced by Cr(III) for leather tanning because Cr(III) is not a carcinogen like Cr(VI), although it is still highly toxic.
Chrome-tanned leather has become an important source of chromium allergy, which affects around 1% of the general population.
Occupational exposure to chromium is common among tannery workers, and a 2008 study found significant chromium in the urine and blood of Kanpur tannery workers.
A 2012 Kanpur survey found that residents of Cr (VI) contaminated communities reported more digestive and skin disorders and blood abnormalities than residents of similar communities without it.
